questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Limit of a Function Involving the Special Limit With Sine
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that as $x\to 0,$ both numerator and denominator approach $0.$

So, if we attempt to evaluate the limit directly, we get

$$
{lim}_{x\to 0}(-\frac{2x}{9\operatorname{sin}⁡x})=\frac{0}{0},
$$

which is an indeterminate form.

Instead, let's recall the following special limit:

$$
{lim}_{x\to 0}\,\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{x}=1
$$

Rewriting the given limit using the algebra of limits and applying our special limit, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}(-\frac{2x}{9\operatorname{sin}⁡x}) & ={lim}_{x\to 0}(-\frac{2}{9}\cdot \frac{x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}) \\  & =-\frac{2}{9}\cdot {lim}_{x\to 0}\,\frac{x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x} \\  & =-\frac{2}{9}\cdot {lim}_{x\to 0}{(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{x})}^{-1} \\  & =-\frac{2}{9}\cdot {[{lim}_{x\to 0}\,\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{x}]}^{-1} \\  & =-\frac{2}{9}\cdot {1}^{-1} \\  & =-\frac{2}{9}\end{aligned}
$$

So, if we attempt to evaluate the limit directly, we get

$$
{lim}_{x\to 0}\,\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x-x}{3x}=\frac{0}{0},
$$

which is an indeterminate form.

Instead, let's recall the following special limit:

$$
{lim}_{x\to 0}\,\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{x}=1
$$

Rewriting the given limit using the algebra of limits and applying our special limit, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\,\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x-x}{3x} & ={lim}_{x\to 0}(\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x-x}{x}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot {lim}_{x\to 0}\,\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x-x}{x} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot {lim}_{x\to 0}(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{x}-\frac{x}{x}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot {lim}_{x\to 0}(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{x}-1) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot [{lim}_{x\to 0}\,\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{x}-{lim}_{x\to 0}\,1] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot (1-1) \\  & =0\end{aligned}

So, if we attempt to evaluate the limit directly, we get

$$
{lim}_{x\to 0}\,\frac{2x+3\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{10x}=\frac{0}{0},
$$

which is an indeterminate form.

Instead, let's recall the following special limit:

$$
{lim}_{x\to 0}\,\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{x}=1
$$

Rewriting the given limit using the algebra of limits and applying our special limit, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\,\frac{2x+3\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{10x} & ={lim}_{x\to 0}(\frac{1}{10}\cdot \frac{2x+3\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{x}) \\  & =\frac{1}{10}\cdot {lim}_{x\to 0}\,\frac{2x+3\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{x} \\  & =\frac{1}{10}\cdot {lim}_{x\to 0}(\frac{2x}{x}+\frac{3\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{x}) \\  & =\frac{1}{10}\cdot {lim}_{x\to 0}(2+3\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{x}) \\  & =\frac{1}{10}\cdot [{lim}_{x\to 0}\,2+3\cdot {lim}_{x\to 0}\,\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{x}] \\  & =\frac{1}{10}\cdot (2+3\cdot 1) \\  & =\frac{5}{10} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Limit of a Function Involving the Special Limit With Sine: Advanced Cases
questions.worked_solution:
First, we can simplify the limit using trigonometric identities, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{4\theta }{\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta \operatorname{tan}⁡\theta } & ={lim}_{\theta \to 0}(4\theta \cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta }) \\  & ={lim}_{\theta \to 0}(4\theta \cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cdot \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }) \\  & ={lim}_{\theta \to 0}(\frac{\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\cdot 4{cos}^{2}⁡\theta ) \\  & ={lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\cdot {lim}_{\theta \to 0}(4{cos}^{2}⁡\theta )\end{aligned}
$$

Let's now evaluate the limits separately:

- Consider the first limit. Notice that as $\theta \to 0,$ both numerator and denominator approach $0.$ 

So, if we attempt to evaluate the limit directly, we get

$$
{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }=\frac{0}{0},
$$

which is an indeterminate form. 

Rewriting the given limit using the algebra of limits and applying our special limit, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } & =\frac{1}{({lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\theta })} \\  & =\frac{1}{1} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

- Consider the second limit. Evaluating it directly, we get

$$
{lim}_{\theta \to 0}(4{cos}^{2}⁡\theta )=4{cos}^{2}⁡0=4.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\cdot {lim}_{\theta \to 0}(4{cos}^{2}⁡\theta ) & =1\cdot 4=4.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Let's now evaluate the limits separately:

- Consider the first limit. Notice that as $\theta \to 0,$ both numerator and denominator approach $0.$ 

So, if we attempt to evaluate the limit directly, we get

$$
{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\theta }=\frac{0}{0},
$$

which is an indeterminate form. 

Instead, let's recall the following special limit:

$$
{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\theta }=1
$$

- Consider the second limit. Evaluating it directly, we get

$$
{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }=\frac{0}{1}=0.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\theta }\cdot {lim}_{\theta \to 0}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } & =1\cdot 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\theta }=0.
$$

$$
{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }=\frac{0}{0},

$$

So, if we attempt to evaluate the limit directly, we get

$$
\displaystyle \lim_{x\to 0}\: \dfrac{2\sin{x}}{3x} = \dfrac{0}{0},
$$

which is an indeterminate form.

Instead, let's recall the following special limit:

$$
\displaystyle \lim_{x\to 0}\: \dfrac{\sin{x}}{x} = 1
$$

Rewriting the given limit using the algebra of limits and applying our special limit, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\,\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{3x} & ={lim}_{x\to 0}(\frac{2}{3}\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{x}) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\cdot {lim}_{x\to 0}\,\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{x} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
